messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test and bug report indicate an infinite loop in HelpFormatter when trying to wrap text that cannot fit within a specified width (in this case, 20 characters). The root cause of this infinite loop lies in the method HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText, which is responsible for wrapping and rendering the given text.

The method renderWrappedText uses findWrapPos to determine where to break the line. If no break position is found (pos == -1), it appends the remaining text and returns. Otherwise, it appends the valid substring and enters a loop to continue with the remaining text.

Inside the loop, if the new wrap position pos is equal to lastPos (the previous wrap position), this indicates that the algorithm cannot advance further, implying the text piece is too long to wrap properly at the required width. Instead of hanging indefinitely, the method throws a RuntimeException with a clear message to avoid infinite looping (related to CLI-162).

This mechanism prevents the infinite loop, but the original bug suggests that before this fix, the code would hang indefinitely because the wrap position never advanced. Thus, the infinite loop occurs because the wrap position calculation fails if a single word is longer than the width, causing the wrapping loop to never move forward.

The failure occurs in printHelp (called by the test), which eventually calls printOptions and renderOptions, where descriptions are passed and fed into renderWrappedText. If the word "looooong" in the description is longer than the set width (20), the wrapping logic fails, causing hanging (before the fix), or an exception now.

Therefore, the infinite loop bug is caused by a missing or improper check in the wrapping logic in renderWrappedText, allowing the wrap position to not advance and looping infinitely.

Relevant code lines confirming this:
- renderWrappedText method lines 822-840 show the loop and the check that throws once no advancement happens.
- The test and bug replicate this by setting width=20 and giving an excessively long word in the description.
- printHelp and printOptions feed descriptions into the wrap logic.
  
Likely the bug was originally caused by lack of the check on pos == lastPos. This is the place where the infinite looping would happen without the exception. The fix is to add this check and throw instead of loop infinitely.

This diagnosis aligns with the current bug report that states infinite looping until JVM crashes with OOM when long words cannot be wrapped, and with the test case triggering it.

Thus, the fault localization is primarily in HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText, specifically around the handling of wrapping positions inside the wrapping loop.

Next, I will suggest which method(s) would be the best locations to fix.
org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText(java.lang.StringBuffer, int, int, java.lang.String)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
